# RAG / Agent / Kafka Oral Drill

[← ByteDance](../README.md) · [Every ByteDance question](../../bytedance.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/rag-agent-kafka-oral-drill)

`concurrency` `kafka` `llm-agent` `networking` `rag` `redis` `tool-use` `verbal`

---

## Requirements

This is a 60-minute technical interview centered on networking and agent systems. The opening half covers fundamentals verbally, while the latter half may involve linked-list coding. Possible discussion areas include:

- RAG system architecture and the candidate’s practical use of it in a project.
- Experience with LangGraph and LangChain, including the structure of the agent framework.
- Agent tool calling, MCP, and the way tools are made available to an agent.
- Agent memory: whether the application retains memories, how they are fetched, and how the system responds when the conversation history grows beyond an extremely large context limit.
- Kafka’s rebalance process.
- Kafka topics, partitions, and consumer groups, including whether separate consumer groups see the same messages.
- Network-layer organization.
- The distinction between concurrency and parallelism.
- Python’s GIL.
- Whether MySQL and Redis are interchangeable, whether Redis supports permanent data retention, and how its persistence is set up.

## Notes

- The interview combines questions about the candidate’s agent project with backend fundamentals. Explain RAG beyond terminology by connecting retrieval, memory, and tool execution to the design of the system you built.
- For oversized contexts, have a specific approach ready: summarize earlier turns, fetch relevant memory fragments, remove low-value context, and keep lasting memory outside the prompt.
- Be exact about Kafka: members of one consumer group divide the partitions among themselves, while distinct consumer groups each get their own copy of the topic stream.

## Preparation

- Reconstruct your RAG or agent design from memory, covering ingestion, embedding, retrieval, reranking, prompt construction, tool calls, and writing memory back.
- Practice explaining consumer groups and rebalancing with a simple example involving partitions and members.
- Prepare brief responses on Redis persistence options, the trade-offs between MySQL and Redis, the Python GIL, and concurrency versus parallelism.
